nina: Quick sync — SMB pilot request from 3 customers: they want predictable latency but can't afford full reserved pools. Sales asks if we can offer a lightweight "mini-pool" (small dedicated slice) as a cheaper on-ramp. Thoughts?
omar: interesting. Implementation options: 1) carve fixed vGPU slices from existing reserved pools (fast), 2) soft-reserve: priority scheduling + admission control (safer), 3) containerized per-tenant instances (more isolation, longer lead time).
tara: option 2 might give the best balance — avoid infra churn and still provide latency isolation guarantees at low cost. We can cap concurrency + prewarm heuristics.
jon: customers need SLA-ish language: 99th under Xms for text-gen bursts < 500 req/min. They prefer productized pricing vs manual credits.
nina: launch criteria proposal: (a) can route customer traffic to mini-pool with per-tenant caps, (b) observability per tenant (latency + tail %), (c) billing attribution per tenant, (d) automated admission/eviction rules. If any fail, we roll back to shared pool.
omar: engineering concerns: admission rules need to play nice with autoscaler. We should add a flag `mini_pool_mode: true` and ensure the autoscaler treats mini-pool capacity as part of shared headroom not new reserved commit.
tara: quick config prototype: 
```json
{"mini_pools": [{"tenant_id":"cust-42","max_concurrency":8,"preferred_regions":["us-west"],"eviction_policy":"least_recent","auto_revoke":"2024-11-30T00:00:00Z"}],"observability":{"per_tenant_metrics":true,"tail_bucket_ms":[50,100,200,500]}}
```
jon: legal and finance will want the wording on "mini-pool" SLAs. Can we commit to a trial SLA that's not contractual? Sales wants to avoid legal for small deals.
nina: agree — treat this as "pilot performance target" not a binding SLA. We'll document in the onboarding email.
omar: timeline: 2 eng weeks to get admission + metrics + billing tags in place if we scope to option 2. Option 1 is faster (few days) but harder to scale. Which do we want?
tara: I'm leaning option 2. Lower operational blast radius and still gives customers predictability. We can mock up for one tenant quickly.
jon: customers would take a quick pilot. One wants it live next Monday. Is that realistic?
omar: for a single pilot tenant maybe — we can flip a route + throttle + billing tag. Full productization needs the 2-week work.
nina: decision: ship a scoped pilot for 1 tenant next week using a manual carve + admission rules; parallel sprint to build the mini-pool feature (option 2) for broader rollout in ~2 weeks.
deploy-bot: ci/pipeline: created branch feature/mini-pool-proto by tara. PR link: https://git.internal/r/changes/13001 awaiting review.
tara: I'll add per-tenant metrics and an oncall dashboard for the pilot, plus an emergency rollback toggle.
omar: I'll draft autoscale exclusion logic and the `mini_pool_mode` flag change. Also will write a short runbook for ops: enrollment, eviction, cost/run-rate checks.
jon: I'll set customer expectations: pilot with performance targets (non-contractual) and weekly check-ins.
nina: action items: tara -> PR + dashboard; omar -> autoscale flag + runbook; legal/finance -> guidance on language for pilot; jon -> customer comms. We'll reconvene Thurs EOD to confirm pilot toggle.
tara: sounds good. no objections.
jon: thumbs up.
nina: thanks team — saving this thread as the decision record for mini-pools pilot.
